questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Croatia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Croatia article.

questions.proof: Its capital and largest city is Zagreb.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Croatia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Croatia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Croatia article.

questions.proof: Croatia is in Central and Southeast Europe, bordering Hungary to the northeast, Serbia to the east, Bosnia and Herzegovina to the south-east, Montenegro to the south-east, the Adriatic Sea to the south-west and Slovenia to the northwest.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Croatia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Croatia article.

questions.proof: Croatia was an independent Catholic kingdom until 1102, when a Hungarian prince inherited the Croatian throne.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Croatia?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Croatia article.

questions.proof: Croatia is a unitary democratic parliamentary republic in Central and Southeastern Europe.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It joined the European Union on 1 July _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Croatia article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: The country's democratic development around 2000, made it possible for Croatia to finally join Slovenia as a European Union member on 1 July 2013.
